sections.content: You know *antes de* and *después de* + infinitive from Unit 4. Use them to organise a travel narrative. *Antes* de + infinitive introduces an action that happens earlier, while *después* de + infinitive introduces an action that happens later. You can combine these with past and recent-experience forms: Antes de *salir*, *preparamos* las *maletas*. Después de *llegar*, *hemos* visitado la *ciudad*.

items.spanish: Antes de salir, preparamos las maletas.
items.english: Before leaving, we prepared the suitcases.

items.spanish: Después de llegar, visitamos la ciudad.
items.english: After arriving, we visited the city.

items.spanish: Antes de viajar, hemos preparado todo.
items.english: Before travelling, we have prepared everything.

items.spanish: Después de volver, hemos recordado el viaje.
items.english: After returning, we have remembered the trip.

sections.content: As in English 'before leaving', Spanish uses the infinitive after *antes de* and *después de* when the subject stays the same: *antes de salir*. When the two halves have different subjects, Spanish needs a full clause instead.
